Are you experiencing any itching, pain, or swelling in addition to the skin changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of outdoor activities and sun exposure, is the rash on your left dorsal hand worse on the side most exposed to the sun? Additionally, have you noticed any blisters, scaling, or changes in the texture of the skin?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential and Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP).
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photos of the left dorsal hand.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is highly unusual; a rough, scaly plaque on the hand is not a symptom of a urinary tract infection, so I would like to correct that impression. To evaluate this properly, can you tell me if this lesion appears to be sun-exposed and if you have noticed any changes in your immune system or recent viral illnesses? REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photos of the left dorsal hand showing the dorsal aspect.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes, Hypertension Social history: Non-smoker, denies alcohol use, enjoys outdoor activities

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your description of a "rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque" on the sun-exposed left dorsal hand, this presentation is highly suspicious for actinic keratosis or squamous cell carcinoma. Given your history of diabetes and significant sun exposure, I need to confirm if you have noticed any recent growth, color change, or bleeding of the lesion. Did the previous doctor perhaps misidentify a skin lesion as a symptom of a urinary tract infection?

speaker: Patient
text: Unremarkable except for the skin condition described

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. Given your age, significant sun exposure, and the description of a rough, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand, this is the most likely diagnosis. I recommend a biopsy of the lesion to rule out progression to squamous cell carcinoma.
